title: Man. Post. Cap. II GAR: Deinde — habitus left in Adam how our hereditary sin?
pass_a_gloss: GAR. Next, by what reason can that habit left in Adam's soul be called our hereditary sin? That habit in Adam's soul—has it not long since ceased to be? How then can it still be, or inhere in us subjectively? Indeed how can one unique habit, that is one and the same accident in number, pass over into so many diverse, and nearly infinite, subjects?
pass_b_english: Garissoles: Next—by what account can that habit left in Adam's soul be called our hereditary sin? Has that habit in Adam's soul not long since ceased to exist? How then can it still be, or inhere in us as in a subject? How can one single habit—one and the same accident in number—pass into so many different subjects, nearly infinite?
source_text: GAR. Deinde, qua ratione habitus ille in Adami anima relictus, dici potest peccatum nostrum haereditarium? habitus ille in Adami anima, nonne diu est cum esse desiit? Quomodo igitur esse amplius potest, aut nobis subjective inhaerere? imo qui fieri potest, ut unicus habitus, id est unum idemque numero accidens, in tam diversa, adeoque infinita pene subjecta transeat?
